actualPromptText:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production game sprite sheet, enemy-044-upp-vanguard, IDLE animation
Primary request: one original fan-made 4 columns by 2 rows sprite sheet, exactly eight chronological idle poses of the same UPP Vanguard.
Backdrop: perfectly flat uniform pure #FF00FF magenta only; no floor, shadow, scenery or grid.
Identity: compact adult human assault elite in strict orthographic side view facing RIGHT. Low shallow rounded helmet with short brow, protected ears, narrow smoked visor, readable jaw, compact left communications block and short antenna. Light-to-medium segmented gray-olive field armor, modest guards, charcoal webbing, compact radio pack, restrained pouches and tiny dull-red functional tab.
Weapon: identical original UPP-pattern pulse/assault rifle in every pose: long straight angular upper receiver, short vented shroud, fixed skeletal stock, curved detachable magazine, compact low optic and short muzzle; complete rifle points RIGHT. Not an M41A or real-world branded rifle.
Style: polished modern 2D metroidvania sprite art, detailed painted pixel-art feel, crisp readable silhouette, original project design.
Composition: exact 2:1 landscape, precise implied 4 columns x 2 rows, exactly eight complete full-body soldiers, generous gutters, identical physical scale and ground line; all equipment fully contained.
Palette: desaturated gray-olive/green-gray, muted sage, charcoal, dark oxidized gunmetal, tiny dull red.
Constraints: stable person, helmet, armor, pouches, rifle geometry, handedness and scale; all right-facing; no text, logo, UI, watermark, crop, overlap or cell contact.
Avoid: USCM/M3/M41A, blue camouflage, AK replica, historical propaganda uniform, glossy armor, exoskeleton, railgun, neon, left-facing, three-quarter camera, weapon morphing or duplicate frames.
Chronology: low-ready neutral; breath in; shoulders rise; tiny scan without turning; peak alert; breath out; weight settles; near-neutral closure. Distinct restrained poses, no steps and no firing.
